commit_message:
[Metal] Fall back to the system default device (#24839)

On an M5 Max running macOS 26.6 inside a Codex sandbox, we observed
`MTLCopyAllDevices()` return an empty array in a fresh process even
though `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()` returned a valid device. IREE
snapshots the first enumeration result when creating its Metal driver,
so an initially empty result leaves that driver permanently without
devices.

Instead, when enumeration is empty, we use the default device as a
one-device fallback.

Fixes #24834.

AI assistance disclosure: I used OpenAI Codex substantially to inspect
the implementation, trace the failure, implement the change, and prepare
this PR (but not write this description). I reviewed and understand the
resulting code and analysis.

commit_message:
[Flow] Bounds-check constant indices in tensor.load/tensor.store folders

TensorLoadOp::fold and TensorStoreOp::fold constant-fold a load from / store
into a constant tensor when the indices are all constant, but neither checks
the constant index against the tensor bounds. getFlattenedIndex (the helper
they use) only asserts a static shape and performs no range validation, and the
op verifiers (TensorLoadOp/TensorStoreOp::verify) only check dynamic dims, not
constant index values. So parseable, verifier-clean IR such as

  %c = flow.tensor.constant dense<[0,1,2,3]> : tensor<4xi32>
  %i = arith.constant 9 : index
  %r = flow.tensor.store %v, %c[%i] : tensor<4xi32>

folds with offset 9 into a 4-element buffer: TensorStoreOp::fold does an
out-of-bounds SmallVector write (assert in asserts builds, heap corruption in
release); TensorLoadOp::fold does the analogous out-of-bounds read.

Add isInBoundsIndex() and bail out of both folds (return {}) on any
out-of-range or wrong-rank constant index. This mirrors the bounds guard added
to the sibling TensorUpdateOp::fold in #24680, which did not cover load/store.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: pr-greeter

commit_message:
[Metal] Fall back to the system default device (#24839)

On an M5 Max running macOS 26.6 inside a Codex sandbox, we observed
`MTLCopyAllDevices()` return an empty array in a fresh process even
though `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()` returned a valid device. IREE
snapshots the first enumeration result when creating its Metal driver,
so an initially empty result leaves that driver permanently without
devices.

Instead, when enumeration is empty, we use the default device as a
one-device fallback.

Fixes #24834.

AI assistance disclosure: I used OpenAI Codex substantially to inspect
the implementation, trace the failure, implement the change, and prepare
this PR (but not write this description). I reviewed and understand the
resulting code and analysis.

---------

Signed-off-by: Jeremy Howard <github@jhoward.fastmail.fm>
name: Analyze (actions)

commit_message:
[Metal] Support queue operations on standalone devices (#24840)

The device-group topology changes in #24248 leave frontier_tracker null
until a device joins a group. PR #24474 added guards for standalone CUDA
and HIP devices, but Metal was omitted. This PR simply adds the
equivalent Metal guard (and a regression test).

Fixes #24835.

commit_message:
[Vulkan] Fix failing allocation on iGPUs (#24736)

If memory requests for HOST_LOCAL memory fail, try to allocate
HOST_VISIBLE/mappable memory.
This is a workaround for what probably would need some refactoring in
the vulkan allocator.

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24717

Co-Authored-By: Claude

If memory requests for HOST_LOCAL memory fail, try to allocate
HOST_VISIBLE/mappable memory.
This is a workaround for what probably would need some refactoring in
the vulkan allocator.

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24717

Co-Authored-By: Claude

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Build] Stop CMake riscv64 defaults from clobbering test cpu-features

platform cmake defaults were appending --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu-features=
after test variants, so the default overwrote +xsmtvdot / VLEN. Do not
override an existing cpu-features flag; prepend missing +m,+a,+f,+d,+c.
Strip those from generator --requirements=.

Signed-off-by: Terence <terrencemahlatini@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Metal] Fall back to the system default device (#24839)

On an M5 Max running macOS 26.6 inside a Codex sandbox, we observed
`MTLCopyAllDevices()` return an empty array in a fresh process even
though `MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()` returned a valid device. IREE
snapshots the first enumeration result when creating its Metal driver,
so an initially empty result leaves that driver permanently without
devices.

Instead, when enumeration is empty, we use the default device as a
one-device fallback.

Fixes #24834.

AI assistance disclosure: I used OpenAI Codex substantially to inspect
the implementation, trace the failure, implement the change, and prepare
this PR (but not write this description). I reviewed and understand the
resulting code and analysis.

---------

Signed-off-by: Jeremy Howard <github@jhoward.fastmail.fm>
name: publish_website

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax, a scalable
pack/unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the inner tile
for any vscale, so verify this and stamp `Multiple` on it.

A pack that consumes an unpack derives its distribution hint from
the unpack's distribution tile.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable pack/unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile, so mmt4d-fused pack/unpack ops (which
distribute on outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) get no
distribution hint, and neither do packs whose scalable dim is not distributed
(e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack).

A pack that consumes an unpack (`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`) derives
its distribution hint from the unpack's distribution tiles, so a pack whose
scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable pack/unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile, so mmt4d-fused pack/unpack ops (which
distribute on outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) get no
distribution hint, and neither do packs whose scalable dim is not distributed
(e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack).

A pack that consumes an unpack (`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`) derives
its distribution hint from the unpack's distribution tiles, so a pack whose
scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_asan / linux_x64_clang_asan

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a

relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for pack

Extends distribution inner-tile alignment hints to pack ops. A scalable pack's
distribution tile is now aligned to base * vscaleMax, so it is a whole multiple
of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

of the runtime inner tile and gets a `distribution` hint of `Multiple`. This
covers both a pack tiled directly and a pack that consumes an unpack
(`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`), which derives its distribution hint
from the unpack's distribution tiles: a match only yields `Multiple` when the
distribution tile is a whole multiple of the pack's largest inner tile, so a
pack whose scalable inner tile differs from its unpack producer's gets no hint.

Packs whose scalable dim is not distributed (e.g. a reduction/broadcast pack)
and mmt4d-fused packs (which distribute on outer dims) are unchanged.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Forward distribution inner-tile alignment hints in forall tiling

Threads the distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints (set on scalable
`linalg.pack`/`linalg.unpack` ops during lowering-strategy selection) into
`TileAndDistributeToWorkgroupsUsingForall`, via
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn(DistributionTiles)` on both the tiling options and the
consumer-fusion step. With a `Multiple` hint the workgroup tiling folds a
scalable/dynamic inner tile to a clean `tile ceildiv innerTile` division instead
of leaving the pack/unpack untiled.

Adds lit coverage: two scalable pack/unpack cases (hint forwarded and preserved
through tiling) and a dynamic-inner-tile case where the hint is load-bearing —
the pack is only tiled into the forall because the hint asserts the multiple
relationship the driver cannot infer from the IR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Set distribution-level inner-tile alignment hints for unpack

After distribution tiles are aligned to base * vscaleMax (see the preceding
change), a scalable unpack's distribution tile is a whole multiple of the
runtime inner tile for any vscale, so record a `distribution` inner-tile
alignment hint of `Multiple` on it.

A distribution tile is classified as `Multiple` only when it is a whole
multiple of the largest inner tile; mmt4d-fused unpacks (which distribute on
outer dims and are not aligned to inner tiles) therefore get no distribution
hint. Pack distribution hints are added separately.

commit_message:
[Metal] Support queue operations on standalone devices (#24840)

The device-group topology changes in #24248 leave frontier_tracker null
until a device joins a group. PR #24474 added guards for standalone CUDA
and HIP devices, but Metal was omitted. This PR simply adds the
equivalent Metal guard (and a regression test).

Fixes #24835.

the implementation and history, implement the change, and prepare the
regression test. I reviewed and understand the resulting code and
analysis, and wrote this description.
